newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds entangled in rollover.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds entangled in rollover.

text.p: *Australian bonds were largely taken up by the rollover of futures contracts ahead of Monday's September expiries and as the market awaited the second stage of key U.S. inflation data.
*Local yield curve steepens further on rate cut hopes.

Australian bonds were largely taken up by the rollover to December futures contracts ahead of Monday's September expiries and as the market awaited the second stage of key U.S. inflation data later on Friday, traders said.

Some domestic selling was seen in early trading, but the short end retained a fairly firm bid as the market again started to build in the possibility of an official interest rate cut before the end of the year.
This caused the local yield curve to extend Thursday's steepening which followed the August labour force report which showed a jump in the unemployment rate to 8.8 percent.

The cash three-/10-year bond yield spread widened to 89 basis points after contracting to 82 from 96 last week when it became clear that the Reserve Bank was not going to ease policy for a second successive monthly board meeting.
However, the market was reluctant to get too carried away on renewed easing hopes with the outlook for U.S. policy still far from clear in the run-up to the September 24 FOMC meeting.

Thursday's release of the August U.S. PPI showed a 0.1 percent fall in the core inflation rate, which has stirred specualtion that the Fed will keep a hike to just 25 basis points, if they tighten at all this time round.
U.S. August CPI is due at 10.30 p.m. (1230 GMT) which is forecast to rise 0.2 percent for both headline and core.
Meanwhile, New Zealand's premium over Australian bond yields widened sharply amid disappointment that the RBNZ failed to ease in its six monthly economic forecasts.
